newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom talks down rights issue, sees higher '96 revenue.
newsitem.headline: Telkom talks down rights issue, sees higher '96 revenue.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Friday it expected revenue growth of 15-25 percent in 1996 and said it had no plans for an additional share flotation.
"Revenue growth this year is expected to be in the range of 15 to 25 percent," Telkom president director and chief executive Asman Akhir Nasution told Reuters in an interview.
Telkom posted operating revenues of 5.11 trillion rupiah ($2.19 billion) in 1995 against 4.04 trillion rupiah in 1994 and 3.07 trillion rupiah in 1993.
It posted operating revenues of 2.38 trillion rupiah in the first half of 1996 against 2.36 trillion rupiah in the same period last year.
Nasution said the first-half results were encouraging but the full year was expected to be better.
"Investment activities usually take place in the first and second quarters of the year and the yields from this investment can usually be reaped in the second half," he said.

Nasution denied speculation that a roadshow by Telkom later this month was an effort to promote the floating of additional shares on overseas markets. He said the firm was in a strong financial condition and had no need to raise fresh funds.
Telkom is listed in London and in New York apart from Jakarta and Surabaya.
"It's up to the government to decide whether to sell additional shares. We don't have the right to make that decision," Nasution said.
The state-owned telecommunications giant plans a roadshow in Japan, Hong Kong, Britain and the United States from September 17 to 27.
"The roadshow aims to promote better understanding between the firm and the public, including our investors and analysts and explaining the progress of the company," Nasution said.

Speculation has surfaced that the government might try to offer additional shares in overseas markets because Telkom scaled down the number offered overseas last year, when its shares were first listed.

Telkom reduced its offshore flotation to around 35 million American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) from an 70 million during the initial offering in October-November 1995. One ADR represents 20 ordinary shares.
Nasution said he was optimistic employees would not sell their allotted shares en masse after a lock-up period ends in November.
"Telkom's employees are proud to hold the shares...they receive good salaries...and they have bought the shares for long-term investment," Nasution said.

Around 40,000 Telkom employees were allocated 116.7 million shares, or around 1.25 percent of the total number offered, during the firm's initial public offer in November 1995. The lock-up period lasted for one year after the listing
Newspaper reports have said many employees are preparing to sell their shares, which they received at 2,050 rupiah each. Telkom was trading at 3,275 rupiah on Friday afternoon, down 50.
